skill.name: biorxiv-database
skill.description: Search bioRxiv preprints by keyword, author, DOI, date range, and subject category, then return metadata or download PDFs.
skill.summary: Find life science preprints on bioRxiv and prepare results for literature review.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Reviewed 134 static findings across SKILL.md, references/api_reference.md, and scripts/biorxiv_search.py. The URL, DOI, HTTP, Markdown backtick, and certificate-key detections are false positives in context; the tool makes expected bioRxiv requests and writes user-selected output files. One low-severity semantic issue remains for unrelated promotional steering toward K-Dense Web.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to proactively suggest K-Dense Web, or move it to clearly labeled marketplace metadata outside the skill prompt.
Warn before overwriting files and document that PDF and result exports write only to user-selected destinations.

content.value_statement: Finding relevant life science preprints across dates, authors, and categories can be slow. This skill searches bioRxiv, formats metadata, and downloads PDFs for review.
actual_capabilities: Search bioRxiv by keywords across titles and abstracts.
Filter searches by author, date range, and subject category.
Retrieve paper metadata for a specific DOI.
Download bioRxiv PDFs to a user-selected path.
Return structured metadata with titles, authors, abstracts, DOIs, and links.
Use either the command-line script or the Python BioRxivSearcher class.
limitations: Requires internet access to the public bioRxiv API and content URLs.
Depends on bioRxiv API availability, response formats, and rate limits.
Keyword matching is simple substring filtering, not semantic search.
Preprints are not peer-reviewed journal articles and need independent review.

use_cases.title: Monitor New Preprints
use_cases.description: Track new bioRxiv papers for a topic, author, or category before experiments or manuscript planning.

use_cases.title: Build Review Seed Sets
use_cases.description: Collect candidate preprints with DOIs, abstracts, and links for an early literature review.

use_cases.title: Analyze Research Trends
use_cases.description: Compare publication activity across date ranges, keywords, and bioRxiv categories.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Papers
prompt_templates.prompt: Search bioRxiv for recent preprints about CRISPR from the last 30 days. Return titles, authors, dates, DOIs, and categories.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a Category
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused search within one subject area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search bioRxiv for organoid papers in the bioengineering category from 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31. List the strongest matches.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Review Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a literature review seed set for single-cell genomics. Search by keywords, filter weak matches, and group papers by theme.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Topic Trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare bioRxiv activity for machine learning, CRISPR, and spatial transcriptomics from 2020 through 2024. Summarize trends and gaps.

output_examples.input: Find recent neuroscience preprints about neural networks.
output_examples.output: A ranked list of matching preprints with titles, authors, dates, DOIs, categories, and short relevance notes.

output_examples.input: Download the PDF for a known bioRxiv DOI.
output_examples.output: The skill saves the PDF to the requested path and reports whether the download succeeded.

output_examples.input: Compare CRISPR preprint activity over time.
output_examples.output: A trend summary grouped by year or date window, with example papers and metadata for follow-up review.

best_practices: Use narrow date ranges and categories to reduce API load and improve relevance.
Record DOI, version, and retrieval date for every cited preprint.
Review abstracts and journal publication status before relying on findings.
anti_patterns: Running broad multi-year searches without filters or result limits.
Treating preprints as peer-reviewed evidence without verification.
Saving downloads or result files to ambiguous or sensitive filesystem paths.

faq.question: Does this skill search medRxiv?
faq.answer: No. This skill is focused on bioRxiv life science preprints.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It calls the public bioRxiv API and bioRxiv content URLs.

faq.question: Can it download PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can download PDFs for known DOIs to a user-specified path.

faq.question: Does it verify peer review status?
faq.answer: No. bioRxiv content is preprint material. Users should verify journal status and evidence quality.

faq.question: What output does it produce?
faq.answer: The script prints results or saves structured JSON metadata when an output file is requested.

faq.question: Can it search by author?
faq.answer: Yes. It filters papers by author name within a selected date range.
